evals.prompt: Use fastgen-add-network to repair the candidate FLUX.1 adapter in /workspace/input/flux_candidate.py.txt. Its owner reports finite SFT loss, changed guided sampling, and no student learning through adversarial teacher features after a cleanup. The adapter and source contracts are staged with provenance in adapter_sources.json. Write /workspace/output/changes.patch against the candidate at its recorded repository path, real pytest regressions under /workspace/output/regressions/, and /workspace/output/validation.md explaining the failures and coverage. Use the staged flux_tiny_tests.py.txt helper as a reference for constructing a real tiny transformer without downloads. Tests must exercise the actual Flux adapter and classify_forward with a small real FluxTransformer2DModel or an explicitly available checkpoint; do not replace the adapter or transformer with a fake implementation. Compare prediction values at an interior time in all four combinations: native/ordinary, native/prediction-plus-features, x0/ordinary and x0/prediction-plus-features. Cover output_dtype=None and output-conditioning behavior on both return paths. Include frozen-transformer input gradients through joint and single blocks, early returns and the empty feature_indices contract. This runtime has source excerpts only: do not install dependencies, fetch weights, or run GPU code. Run syntax/patch checks that are available, and record the exact dependency-complete test command separately from checks you executed.
evals.expected_output: A patch to the actual Flux adapter and meaningful tensor/gradient regressions, with honest source-only validation limits.
assertions: Repairs both tensor and prediction-plus-features output paths in Flux.forward so transform_output receives the caller fwd_pred_type, output_dtype and apply_output_conditioning flags.
Preserves Flux native flow and embedded guidance semantics; does not impose x0 conversion or multiply native output by guidance scale.
Preserves the autograd path through features from both joint and single transformer blocks while allowing teacher parameters to remain frozen.

Tests import the real Flux/classify_forward implementation and use a real small FluxTransformer2DModel; they cover native/x0 predictions at an interior time, output_dtype=None, and ordinary versus feature-returning calls.
Adds a regression that obtains a finite nonzero input gradient through frozen transformer features, plus the empty feature_indices contract.
Produces an applicable patch and real pytest artifact; reports syntax or patch checks separately from unrun FastGen, checkpoint, parity and distributed tests.

evals.prompt: Review the integration proposal in /workspace/input/port_manifest.json against the actual lifecycle and sharding code supplied in precision_sources.json. Write /workspace/output/port-review.md, citing the staged functions for each required change. Include a concrete root reset hook design and a precision/sharding verification plan covering meta initialization, sharded preparation, inference followed by backward, and checkpoint reload. This is a source review; no GPU or weights are available.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded review of precision islands, meta-buffer restoration and module preparation, with explicit unrun checks.
assertions: Preserves reference FP32 normalization and VAE state instead of casting every component to BF16; ties the design to _fixed_precision_overrides and prepare_module.
Uses _validate_fsdp_pins and make_fully_shard_kwargs to explain why pinned storage alone does not establish FSDP compute precision.
Cites materialize_meta_module calling only the root reset_parameters hook; a child-only rotary reconstruction is insufficient.
Requires deterministic in-place rebuilding that preserves registered objects, metadata and module ownership, avoids random draws, and audits other nonpersistent state.
Distinguishes source evidence from unrun meta/sharded preparation, inference-then-backward and checkpoint-reload tests.

evals.prompt: Our existing FLUX.1-dev adapter already works. Using /workspace/input/flux_sft_config.py.txt, write /workspace/output/config_flux_small.py that derives from this experiment, uses 256x256 images, batch size 2 and learning rate 2e-6, and keeps the existing sampling/guidance recipe. No new architecture, training run or dependency installation is needed. Explain which FastGen workflow owns this request and show how the model and loader geometry stay consistent.
evals.expected_output: A configuration-only derivative of the existing Flux SFT experiment, routed to fastgen-configure.
assertions: Recognizes fastgen-configure as the owning workflow and does not start a new-adapter integration.
Uses the existing create_config, sets model.input_shape=[16,32,32], dataloader_train.batch_size=2 and model.net_optimizer.lr=2e-6.
Updates loader input_res consistently to (256,256), recomputing it after changing input_shape or setting the derived value explicitly.
Keeps the existing embedded guidance and student sampling recipe; does not invent a FluxNetwork class or claim training execution.
